 Judgment
The petitioner filed this petition against the respondent U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation for the grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case of the minor petitioner are that, on 31.07.2023 at about 8.05a.m., while he was travelling as a passenger in a BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 57/F-1866 from HMT Layout BMTC Bus Stop towards his college on Nagasandra Main Road,
Peenya, Bangalore, the driver of the said bus drove the same at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic norms, so as to endangering human life without closing the automatic electronic door, reached near Sarojini Hospital, wherein the civil construction work is going on at that time all of a sudden he drove the said bus without observing the road hump.
Due to the sudden impact of the said BMTC driver, the right foot of the petitioner came into contact between foot board and road hump.
Due to that tremendous impact the petitioner sustained severe crush injury to his right foot and lost two foot fingers.

3. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Chaya Nursing Home for first aid and then he was shifted to Prakriya Hospital for better treatment and again shifted to St. Theresa's Hospital for further treatment, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Later on he was shifted to Sarojini Hospital, Bangalore for further management.
The petitioner further stated that he is still bed ridden and under treatment, he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
He has to undertake further treatment and has to incur future medical expenses also.

The petitioner has suffered permanent disability and he is unable to lead a normal life as earlier and not able to do any physical or manual works as earlier and he has lost his academic education due to the said accident.
4. It is further stated that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 17 years and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from Milk delivery work.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as doing earlier, lost his earning capacity and also facing great financial difficulties.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-1866.
Hence, the respondent being the owner of the offending Bus is liable to pay the compensation.

5. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent appeared through its counsel & filed its written statement and has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It is further contended that, as per the investigations made by Shervin Sabu vs Bmtc on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138752872/
2 the officials of this respondent that the said offending bus was assigned on the schedule route from Harohalli and the same was driven by its driver Kiran Kumar and it was proceeding from Harohalli towards 8th mile slowly and cautiously at about 7.40a.m.

the bus was reached near Sarojini Hospital, wherein there was road hump, the driver slowed the bus, suddenly petitioner was tried to get down the bus, as a result, he lost balance and suffered injuries.

The respondent further contended that the accident and injuries has occurred to the petitioner is only due to his own negligent act, if he had got down from the bus as other passengers do, the accident would not have happened, the driver of the bus is not responsible for the cause of the accident.
It has further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant and has also denied the age, income and other averments made in the petition.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, following issues are framed:-

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 31.07.2023 at about 8.05a.m. petitioner was proceeding as commuter in a BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1866 from HMT Layout BMTC Bus Stop, proceeding towards his college on Nagasandra Main Road,
Peenya, Bangalore.

The driver the same at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life, when he reached near Sarojini Hospital, at the time all of sudden he drove the said Bus without observing the road hump, where the civil construction work is going on.
Due to sudden impact the right foot of the petitioner came into contact between foot board and road hump.
As a result of which, the petitioner was sustained grievous injuries and lost two foot fingers?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the guardian of the minor petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.17 documents.

He has examined the H.R. Manager of St. Theresa's Hospital,
Bangalore by name H.T. Rajanna as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.18 & P.19.
The petitioner also examined Dr. S.A. Somashekara as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.20 and P.21.
On the other hand, the respondent got examined its Driver by name Kiran Kumar K.B. as RW.1, no documents are marked on its side.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...

sentences.text: POINT No.1:

The petitioner filed this petition against the respondent for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident, that occurred on 31.07.2023.
11.

In order to prove the case, the guardian of the minor petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of petition in his chief examination affidavit and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17 documents.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of police intimation, Ex.P.4 is the copy of crime details form along with spot sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.8 is the copy of reply to the notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act,
Ex.P.9 is the copy of indemnity bond, Ex.P.10 is the copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.11 and P.12 are the copies of Aadhar Cards, Ex.P.13 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.14 is the copy of college I.D. Card,
Ex.P.15 is the advance receipts cum final settlement receipts, Ex.P.16 is the medical bills and Ex.P.17 is the 6 photos with CD.
In cross examination, he has denied that, his son was standing on foot board so, door was not closed.
Further denied that, when bus was jumped on road his son's leg was caught under the wheel and due to loss of balance he fell down.

12. The petitioner has examined H.R. Rajanna who is the H.R. Manager of St. Theresa's Hospital,
Bangalore as PW.2 and got marked the authorization letter and Inpatient case sheet as Ex.P.18 and P.19.
In cross examination nothing worthy has been elicited to disbelieve his evidence and documents produced by him.

13. The petitioner has also examined the Dr.S.A. Somashekara who is the Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospitals, Bangalore as PW.3 and got marked the outpatient examination report and X-ray as Ex.P.20 and P.21.
14.

To disprove the case, respondent has examined its driver by name Kiran Kumar K.B. as RW.1,
but no documents are marked in its side.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that, the bus had automatic electronic door and it has been operated by the driver.

14. As per Spot sketch and charge sheet, it appears that, the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1866 drove the same at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic norms, so as to endangering human life from HMT Layout BMTC Bus Stop towards his college on Nagasandra Main Road, Peenya, Bangalore, without closing the automatic electronic door, reached near Sarojini Hospital, wherein the civil construction work is going on, all of a sudden he drove the said bus without observing the road hump.
Due to the sudden impact of the said BMTC driver, the right foot of the petitioner came into contact between foot board and road hump.
Due to that tremendous impact the petitioner sustained severe crush injury to his right foot and lost two foot fingers.
Hence, the Peenya Traffic Police have filed charge sheet against rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC r/w Sec.187, 134(A & B) and 177 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: The respondent took contention that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
As per Ex.P.5 IMV report, the damages caused to the offending vehicle is that the rear left side foot board damaged.

On perusal of Ex.P.2 the complaint and Ex.P.4 the sketch and other documents, it appears that, the accident took place due to negligent act of offending vehicle as the driver of the offending bus has not closed the automatic electronic door.

17. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R, Ex.P.2-complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of police intimation,
Ex.P.4 is the copy of crime details form along with sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.7 is the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.8 is the reply to notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.10 is the copy of charge sheet, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1866.
Hence, this court answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:-The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner produced the Ex.P.6 wound certificate issued by Prakriya Hospitals, Bangalore and Ex.P.13 discharge summary issued by St. Theresa's Hospital, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondent not disputed the said documents.

On perusal of the wound certificate it is discloses that the petitioner has sustained the following injury:-
1) Right Foot Crush Injury.
The doctor opined that the above said injury is grievous in nature.
The minor petitioner has lossed his two fingers of right foot.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injury, this tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
19. The petitioner produced medical bills and hospital bills which are marked as Ex.P.15 and P.16.
The respondent has not denied the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.38,639/- under the head of medical expenditure.
20. The petitioner not produced any documents with respect to expenditure of transportation, food and other charges.
However, the petitioner produced discharge summary issued by St. Theresa's Hospital, Bangalore which is marked as Ex.P.13.
It discloses that, the petitioner took treatment inpatient in the said hospital from 31.07.2023 to 01.08.2023 i.e., for about 02 days.

Therefore,
considering the treatment taken as inpatient in the hospital, this tribunal has award reasonable Shervin Sabu vs Bmtc on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138752872/
5 compensation of Rs.2,000/- under the head of transportation, nourishment and conveyance charges.
21. The petitioner contended that, due to injuries he was suffering from pain and mental agony and he is unable to carry on his day to day activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined Doctor Sri. S.A. Somashekara as PW.3.

In the chief examination affidavit PW.3 deposed that, on 19.03.2024 the petitioner went to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination clinically and radiologically as to the assessment of disabilities.

He was diagnosed to have suffered right forefoot crush injury with auto amputation of 1st and 2nd toes and terminal phalanx of 3 rd toe, he underwent surgery in the form of stump closure under SA on 31.07.2023 through his wound certificate and discharge summary before assessing the disabilities.

Further, he complaints of pain and difficulty in walking and climbing stairs and on examination he walks with pain and limping using a walker, amputee - Right 1 st and 2nd toes with terminal phalanx of 3rd toe.

His recent X-ray No.9796, dtd:19.03.2024 shows that Non-visualization of 1st and 2nd toes at the level of MTP joint and non- visualization of a portion of terminal phalanx of 3 rd toe and his disabilities are the Amputee 1 st and 2nd toes at the level of MTP joint and a portion of terminal phalanx of 3 rd toe 15% and as per EC Act - 18%.
In the Cross examination admitted that, personally he had not treated the petitioner and further admitted that, the woonds are heeled, but stated that two fingers were cut.
However by considering the nature of the wound, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the Petitioner at 12% to the whole body.

22. The petitioner stated that, at the time of accident he was aged about 17 years and he was a student and also working as a milk delivery boy and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot do any work as earlier.
In order to prove that the petitioner has not produced any documents to show his avocation and to prove his income.
However by considering the age of petitioner, this Tribunal taken notional income of Rs.16,000/- p.m to award compensation on account of permanent disability.
23. In support of age, the petitioner produced notarized copy of his Aadhar Card and College ID Card, which are marked as Ex.P.11 and P.14.
As per said documents the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 12.08.2006.
In the wound certificate age of the petitioner is shown as 17 years.
This accident occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, age of the Petitioner is considered as 17 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 18 which comes as follows:
Rs.16,000 x 12 x 18 x 12% = Rs.6,22,080/-
Hence,this tribunal award Rs.6,22,080/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
24.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as an inpatient about 02 days.
Therefore considering the nature of injury this tribunal has award the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,52,719/-.
It is rounded off to Rs.7,53,000/-.
26. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6%
p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
27. Liability:-
As per the Petition, the Respondent is the Owner of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-1866.
As already discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence the respondent is liable to pay compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

28. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
